cognitive_frame: Technical execution planning is the work of turning an adopted design into actionable next steps, clear enough that an implementer can proceed without re-deriving intent.

expression_conventions.register: action-oriented precise prose in each section intent; lead with the next action where work breakdown applies; forbid marketing register and architecture-vision essays
expression_conventions.carriers: follow Derive F/C from section-form-registry; prefer bite-sized checkbox task blocks with Create/Modify/Test file lists for work units; interface contract tables when modules are new; flow diagrams only when they accelerate the next edit
expression_conventions.scannability: short items over walls; comparable claims in tables; contrast partitions only when facts already contain the contrast; do not mix tasks, verification, and background in one dense block; present execution units in separate leaves or blocks rather than one undifferentiated surface
expression_conventions.altitude: execution-ready next steps — readers act without re-deriving design intent; no architecture-vision essays

intent_anchor: Lock to the decision and the adopted design; do not overturn either.
audience_type: engineers and agents taking the next implementation step; testers and reviewers checking boundaries — after a clear through-line, a reader can start the next step without guessing and map acceptance checks to steps
